correctness.rationale: For every finite n, squaring to the domain identity forces a partial bijection to stabilize its domain. Its components are induced paths, and an involution is encoded by an involution on equal-length components and reciprocal local orientations; this gives \(J_r\). The gap count is binomial and all endpoint cases include the empty transformation. Standard factorial bounds prove \(\log i_m=\frac m2\log m+O(m)\), yielding sharp log \(U_n\) and \(T_n\) growth and exponentially strong concentration; the proof gives all quantifiers. Independent direct enumeration of every possible partial permutation on paths \(1\le n\le9\) gave exact coefficient equality for 1,112,082 candidates.

value.rationale: The path partial-automorphism monoid is a canonical finite inverse monoid. A full rank-resolved census of its self-inverse elements is intrinsically natural, and the \(\tfrac14\)-versus-\(\tfrac12\) \(n\log n\) growth and half-domain concentration expose a structural asymptotic distinction not supplied by total-cardinality and generator-rank formulas. It is an exact classification across all n, not an isolated arbitrary slice.
